reader_notes: Short single-question unit; period vocabulary (draper's, day-books, to let) is contextually recoverable and adds authentic texture.

Option B is well-built: the passage does say the upper-floor counters suddenly out-took the ground floor, but explicitly says the novelty wore off within a few years, so 'permanently' is refuted by the text rather than merely unmentioned.
The historian's own hedge ('wary of drawing a rule from a single shop') is present and does not undercut the keyed reading, which is scoped to the first two seasons by the stem.
